docs.title: Pyragify
docs.text:
Pyragify exports local repository source as Markdown with a provenance manifest. Each selected UTF-8 file appears once, without semantic extraction or whitespace normalization. The index links to source blocks and lists intentional omissions.

pyragify process-repo --repo-path ./my-project --output-dir ./output --no-enable-graph

Open output/index.md, then inspect the source parts and metadata.json before sharing them. Ignore rules are not secret detection. Source read failures and word-limit violations fail the export before publication.

Start with the quick start, configuration, and output contract. The Repomix comparison explains the remaining reason for a custom exporter.

Knowledge graphs are a separate, experimental output. They may omit or misidentify relationships. Source retention does not require their parsers. NotebookLM ingestion, LLM answer quality, and large-repository performance have not been evaluated.

For development, see contributing and the API reference.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to Pyragify will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Bundle pyragify-export and pyragify-graph agent skills with the Python package for discovery and installation through Library Skills.
  • Verify skill contents, executable examples, release archives, and isolated consumer installations locally and in test CI. PyPI publication is a separate step; versions before 0.5.0 do not include the bundled skills.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Require Python 3.12 only (>=3.12,<3.13), with locked installation in test CI.
  • Replace tree-sitter-languages with official Tree-sitter 0.26.1 bindings and individually pinned grammars for JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C, C++, Go, HTML, and CSS. Python analysis still uses the standard-library ast module.
  • Cache version 10 rebuilds records from version 9 and earlier on the next export.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• JavaScript and TypeScript inheritance queries use each grammar's node shapes and parser positions to identify subclasses sharing a source line.
  • JavaScript and TypeScript superclass resolution respects lexical shadowing and leaves uncertain bindings unresolved.
  • C files no longer execute C++ class queries; dependency query failures log warnings.
  • Regression checks cover resource declarations (using and await using), including initializer ownership, shadowing, and block scope.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Complete source exports with a provenance manifest, source hashes, and line mappings.
  • Resolution of explicit Python function imports and aliases in root and src/ layouts.
  • JavaScript and TypeScript arrow-function callers and callees, including nested callbacks.
  • A reproducible synthetic graph benchmark with recorded results and limitations.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Graph queries build a temporary adjacency map; cross-file resolution shares import indexes.
  • Cache version 8 rebuilds records created by earlier graph extractors.
  • Graphs remain experimental and opt-in. Dynamic calls, re-export chains, and JavaScript module resolution remain unsupported.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Python shadowed names no longer resolve to unrelated local functions.
  • Definition defaults and decorators retain their containing execution owner.
  • JavaScript and TypeScript calls use parser positions, including same-line definitions and CRLF input.
  • Documentation deployment uses the locked docs dependency group on Python 3.12.
  • Export safety, CLI query validation, and relationship traversal fixes accumulated since 0.2.0.

def process_repository(
    repo_path: Path,
    output_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
    max_words: int = 200000
) -> List[Path]:

        max_words: Maximum words per output chunk

from pyragify.processor import FileProcessor

class TestFileProcessor:
    def test_python_chunking(self, tmp_path):
        """Test that Python files are chunked correctly."""
        # Arrange
        processor = FileProcessor(tmp_path, tmp_path / "output")
        test_file = tmp_path / "test.py"
        test_file.write_text("""
def hello_world():
    '''A simple function.'''

""")

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Provide a source directory through YAML or --repo-path. The CLI reads config.yaml in the current directory by default. Use --config-file to choose another file; no other filenames or environment variables are searched.

repo_path: .
output_dir: ./output
max_words: 200000
max_file_size: 10485760
skip_patterns: ["*.log", "*.tmp"]
skip_dirs: [node_modules, __pycache__]
verbose: false
graph:
  enabled: false
  output_dir: graphs

docs.title: Supported settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning repo_path Required Source directory output_dir ./output Dedicated Markdown and manifest output directory max_words 200000 Positive hard word limit per Markdown file, including formatting; oversized files or index fail max_file_size 10485760 Maximum source size in bytes skip_patterns Built-in image patterns and .git Additional patterns, using gitignore syntax skip_dirs [node_modules, __pycache__] Directory names to exclude; an empty list also uses these defaults verbose false Enable debug logging graph.enabled false Build the experimental repository graph graph.output_dir graphs Graph directory; relative paths are under output_dir graph.format json Only JSON is supported

Relationship filtering, compression, and configuration switches for graph resolution, validation, repair, or traversal depth are not implemented. Graph-enabled processing rejects unsupported settings instead of ignoring them. Use query-graph --depth to control related-context traversal.

docs.title: Command-line overrides
docs.text:
pyragify process-repo --config-file config.yaml --repo-path ./my-project \
  --output-dir ./export --max-words 100000 --verbose --enable-graph

pyragify process-repo --repo-path ./my-project \
  --skip-patterns '*.log' --skip-patterns '*.tmp' \
  --skip-dirs node_modules --skip-dirs __pycache__

Repeat list options rather than joining values with commas. See the CLI reference for all options.

docs.title: Incremental processing
docs.text: Unchanged files reuse versioned cached chunks and graph data. Exports are rebuilt from all current records, including unchanged files. Deleted sources disappear. To force reprocessing, remove .pyragify-cache.json from your configured output_dir and run the same command again. hashes.json is an inspection artifact, not the processing cache.

docs.title: Safe paths and export failures
docs.text:
Use dedicated output directories. Text output and graph output must not equal or contain the source repository. Output paths and artifact destinations containing symlinks are rejected. Relative graph output paths are resolved under output_dir; an absolute graph output path is used directly. Both locations are excluded from source discovery.

In a Git working tree, discovery uses Git's tracked and untracked file list with standard ignore rules. Nested .gitignore rules, configured skip patterns, root .dockerignore, size limits, and binary filtering also apply. File and directory symlinks are excluded. Git submodules and nested untracked repositories are not recursively exported.

Without Git discovery, Pyragify walks directories without following symlinks, honors root and nested .gitignore files, and prunes ignored directories before reading their children. Git global ignores and .git/info/exclude are not used in this fallback. Pruned directories are recorded as directory exclusions rather than a list of every file beneath them. Git-ignored paths are recorded from Git, using compact directory entries that cover their descendants. The index and manifest also record generated-output directories and repository metadata as omissions. These filters are not a secret scanner; inspect exports before sharing them.

Replacement text, graph, metadata, hashes, and cache files are prepared before publication. Serialization or write errors fail the command; ordinary publication errors restore previous artifact contents. Source read/worker failures are reported separately from exclusions and abort publication. A missing or invalid optional cache triggers processing again; malformed graph query inputs fail.

.pyragify-artifacts.json records owned Markdown parts (and recognizes owned legacy text parts). Only previously listed chunks are removed when obsolete. Old exports without this list may leave stale chunks; inspect those files and remove them manually. Current chunk names and standard JSON artifact names are reserved for Pyragify in the output directories. Keep unrelated files elsewhere. Do not run concurrent exports into the same output directories. Rollback handles raised errors, not process termination or power loss during publication.

Graph symbols carry enclosing scopes, so A.run and B.run have separate identities. Hierarchy queries accept a bare name, a qualified name, or a node ID. Python dependency queries resolve exact module paths at the repository root or under src/, including relative imports. Custom import roots and dynamic receivers remain unresolved. Cross-file edges require explicit imports.

The graph remains experimental: these safety guarantees do not establish correct relationships. Source retention is separate and complete for every selected UTF-8 file; see the output contract. Source-only exports do not use parsers. Do not edit sources during a run or expect repository-wide snapshot isolation.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This guide will help you install Pyragify on your system.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python: Version 3.12 only (>=3.12,<3.13)
  • Operating System: Linux, macOS, or Windows

docs.title: Method 1: Using uv (Recommended)
docs.text:
uv is a fast Python package manager that handles virtual environments automatically.

# Install uv if you don't have it
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Install Pyragify
uv pip install pyragify

docs.title: Method 2: Using pip
docs.text:
If you prefer using pip, you can install Pyragify from PyPI:

# Install Pyragify
pip install pyragify

# Optional: Create a virtual environment first
python -m venv pyragify-env
source pyragify-env/bin/activate  # On Windows: pyragify-env\Scripts\activate
pip install pyragify

docs.title: Method 3: From Source
docs.text:
If you want to install from source (for development or the latest features):

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/ThomasBury/pyragify.git
cd pyragify

# Install with uv (recommended)
uv sync --locked --group dev --group docs

# Or with pip
pip install -e .

docs.title: Agent skills
docs.text:
Pyragify 0.5.0 bundles two self-contained skills: pyragify-export covers source-only exports and manifest inspection; pyragify-graph covers experimental graph export and queries with source checks. Versions before 0.5.0 do not contain them. Once 0.5.0 or later is available on your package index, install from a consuming project using Python 3.12:

uv add --dev pyragify
uvx library-skills install --skill pyragify-export --skill pyragify-graph
uvx library-skills scan --json

PyPI publication is separate from the GitHub release. Until the package is on your index, use the 0.5.0 release wheel URL so other developers and CI can sync the same dependency:

uv add --dev https://github.com/ThomasBury/pyragify/releases/download/0.5.0/pyragify-0.5.0-py3-none-any.whl

uv records that wheel URL under [tool.uv.sources], so normal upgrades keep using the same wheel. After 0.5.0 or later is available on your package index, remove only the pyragify entry from [tool.uv.sources] in pyproject.toml, then run uv lock --upgrade-package pyragify and uv sync --python 3.12 to resolve and install from the index.

Both commands assume the consuming project's declared requires-python is >=3.12,<3.13. uv resolves against that entire range, not just the interpreter currently running. If your project supports other Python versions, add --marker 'python_version == "3.12"' to either uv add command to limit this development dependency to Python 3.12. The marker does not select an interpreter. Before adding the dependency, select Python 3.12 for the project environment:

uv python pin 3.12
uv sync --python 3.12

Then run the chosen uv add command with the marker. Use uv run pyragify for exports; uvx library-skills scans the project's now-synced .venv. See uv's resolution rules.

Library Skills discovers skills inside installed library packages. It scans the project's environment, so a global installation or an isolated uvx pyragify CLI alone does not support this workflow. Run discovery and installation from the project root with its environment synced.

The default targets are .agents/skills/pyragify-export and .agents/skills/pyragify-graph. The official CLI options include --claude to install additional targets under .claude/skills and --copy to create ordinary directories where symlinks are unavailable:

uvx library-skills install --skill pyragify-export --skill pyragify-graph --claude
# Alternative for environments without symlinks:
uvx library-skills install --skill pyragify-export --skill pyragify-graph --copy

Symlinked skills follow the installed package version. Copied skills require refreshing after upgrades: remove the old copied skill directories and reinstall with --copy, preserving any local edits separately.

To use a source checkout containing these skills:

git clone https://github.com/ThomasBury/pyragify.git
cd pyragify
uv sync --locked
uvx library-skills scan --all --json
uvx library-skills install --skill pyragify-export --skill pyragify-graph

--all includes the checkout package itself, which is not one of its own declared dependencies. In a consuming project, the default scan includes Pyragify because it is a declared dependency.

The local packaging check uses Library Skills 0.0.19 against isolated wheel, editable, and source-distribution installations:

uv run --locked python scripts/check_skill_packaging.py

Installation from PyPI remains unverified until PyPI publication.

docs.text:

Do not upgrade them independently. Python analysis continues to use the standard-library ast module.

For a source checkout containing pyproject.toml and uv.lock, install the locked dependencies from the checkout root:

uv sync --locked

This command is for repository development, not for a standalone pip installation.

After installation, choose a source directory and a dedicated output directory. From a source checkout:

uv run pyragify process-repo --repo-path ./my-project --output-dir ./output --no-enable-graph

The CLI reads config.yaml in the current directory by default. Options override its values. To save a repeatable configuration:

repo_path: ./my-project
output_dir: ./output
max_words: 200000
max_file_size: 10485760
skip_patterns: ["*.log"]
skip_dirs: [node_modules, __pycache__]
graph:
  enabled: false

uv run pyragify process-repo --config-file config.yaml

Open output/index.md. Follow the file links to complete source blocks, use their paths and source line ranges to locate definitions, and read the omissions list. metadata.json maps the same files to parts, source hashes, and exact output byte ranges. Included source appears once; imports, decorators, async code, comments, and Markdown headings are retained.

Every generated Markdown file must fit max_words, including its headers and the index. Files are indivisible. If a source file or the index cannot fit, processing fails with a message to increase the limit or reduce the selection. The limit counts whitespace-separated words, not model tokens.

Run the same command after editing your repository. Unchanged files reuse the cache, and deleted files disappear from the new handoff. A failed export leaves the previous published handoff intact for ordinary raised errors. Do not edit sources or run concurrent exports during processing.

Graph building is optional and experimental:

uv run pyragify process-repo --config-file config.yaml --enable-graph
uv run pyragify query-graph --graph-path output/graphs/repository_graph.json --command stats

Graphs are outside the trusted source handoff. Inspect selected files before sharing; filtering is not secret detection. No particular chat service's acceptance or answer quality is guaranteed.

See configuration, the CLI reference, and the output contract for details.

@app.command()
def process_repo(
    config_file: Path = typer.Option("config.yaml", help="Path to the configuration YAML file."),
    repo_path: Path = typer.Option(None, help="Override: Path to the repository to process."),
    output_dir: Path = typer.Option(None, help="Override: Directory to save output files."),
    max_words: int = typer.Option(None, help="Positive word limit per Markdown file, including headers. Oversized files fail."),
    max_file_size: int = typer.Option(None, help="Override: Maximum file size to process (in bytes)."),
    skip_patterns: list[str] = typer.Option(None, help="Override: List of file patterns to skip."),
    skip_dirs: list[str] = typer.Option(None, help="Override: List of directories to skip."),
    verbose: bool = typer.Option(None, help="Override: Enable verbose output."),
    enable_graph: bool = typer.Option(None, help="Override: Enable experimental graph output (outside the source handoff)."),
    graph_output_dir: str = typer.Option(None, help="Override: Directory to save graph files."),
    graph_format: str = typer.Option(None, help="Override: Graph serialization format (only json is supported)."),
    include_relationships: list[str] = typer.Option(None, help="Unsupported: relationship filtering is not implemented.")
) -> None:
    """
    Export complete UTF-8 source, a Markdown index, and metadata.json.

    This command processes a repository using a configuration file and optional command-line overrides. 
    Each source file is retained once. A file or index that cannot fit the word limit fails before publication.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config_file : pathlib.Path, optional
        The path to the configuration YAML file. Default is "config.yaml".
    repo_path : pathlib.Path, optional
        Override for the path to the repository to process. Defaults to the value in the configuration file.
    output_dir : pathlib.Path, optional
        Override for the directory where output files will be saved. Defaults to the value in the configuration file.
    max_words : int, optional
        Override for the maximum number of words allowed per output file. Defaults to the value in the configuration file.
    max_file_size : int, optional
        Override for the maximum file size (in bytes) to process. Defaults to the value in the configuration file.
    skip_patterns : list of str, optional
        Override for the list of file patterns to skip (e.g., "*.log", "*.tmp"). Defaults to the value in the configuration file.
    skip_dirs : list of str, optional
        Override for the list of directory names to skip (e.g., "node_modules", "__pycache__"). Defaults to the value in the configuration file.
    verbose : bool, optional
        Override for enabling verbose output. When enabled, the logging level is set to DEBUG. Defaults to the value in the configuration file.

    Notes
    -----
    - If a configuration file exists, its settings are loaded first.
    - Command-line options take precedence and override corresponding configuration file values.
    - The repository is processed based on the final resolved configuration, and results are saved to the specified output directory.
    - Errors during processing are logged, and the command exits with an error code.

    Examples
    --------
    Run the command with the default configuration file:
        $ python -m yourmodule.cli process-repo

    Override the repository path and enable verbose output:
        $ python -m yourmodule.cli process-repo --repo-path /path/to/repo --verbose

    Specify a custom configuration file:
        $ python -m yourmodule.cli process-repo --config-file custom_config.yaml
    """

    # Load configuration from YAML
    if config_file.exists():
        config = OmegaConf.load(config_file)
        logger.info(f"Loaded configuration from '{config_file}'")
    else:
        config = OmegaConf.create()
        if repo_path is None: # No --repo-path override
            logger.error(f"Configuration file '{config_file}' not found and --repo-path not provided.")
            raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    # Apply CLI overrides
    overrides = {
        "repo_path": repo_path,
        "output_dir": output_dir,
        "max_words": max_words,
        "max_file_size": max_file_size,
        "skip_patterns": skip_patterns,
        "skip_dirs": skip_dirs,
        "verbose": verbose,
    }
    for key, value in overrides.items():
        if value is not None:
            config[key] = value

    # Handle graph configuration
    if "graph" not in config:
        config["graph"] = {}

    graph_overrides = {
        "enabled": enable_graph,
        "output_dir": graph_output_dir,
        "format": graph_format,
        "relationships": include_relationships,
    }
    for key, value in graph_overrides.items():
        if value is not None:
            config["graph"][key] = value

    if _config_value(config, "verbose", False):
        logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
        logger.debug("Verbose mode enabled. Setting logging level to DEBUG.")

    # Validate repo_path after config is loaded and merged
    resolved_repo_path = _config_value(config, "repo_path")
    if not resolved_repo_path:
        typer.echo("Error: repo_path must be defined in the config file or via --repo-path.", err=True)
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    repo_path_obj = Path(resolved_repo_path)
    if not repo_path_obj.exists():
        typer.echo(f"Error: Repository path '{resolved_repo_path}' does not exist.", err=True)
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)
    if not repo_path_obj.is_dir():
        typer.echo(f"Error: Repository path '{resolved_repo_path}' is not a directory.", err=True)
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    graph_config = _plain_dict(_config_value(config, "graph", {}))

    processor_kwargs = {
        "repo_path": repo_path_obj,
        "output_dir": Path(_config_value(config, "output_dir", "./output") or "./output"),
        "enable_graph": graph_config.get("enabled", False),
        "graph_config": graph_config,
    }
    for key in ("max_words", "max_file_size", "skip_patterns", "skip_dirs"):
        value = _config_value(config, key)
        if value is not None:
            processor_kwargs[key] = value

    # Initialize and run the processor
    try:
        processor = RepoContentProcessor(**processor_kwargs)
        processor.process_repo()
        logger.info("Repository processing completed successfully!")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"An error occurred during repository processing: {e}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

@app.command()
def query_graph(
    graph_path: Path = typer.Option(None, help="Path to the knowledge graph JSON file."),
    command: str = typer.Option(..., help="Query command to execute."),
    entity: str = typer.Option(None, help="Entity ID or name for queries."),
    depth: int = typer.Option(2, help="Traversal depth for related context."),
    pattern: str = typer.Option(None, help="Search pattern for pattern matching."),
    output_format: str = typer.Option("json", help="Output format (json, text).")
) -> None:
    """
    Query the knowledge graph for context and relationships.

    Available commands:
    - related: Find related context for an entity
    - hierarchy: Get call hierarchy for a function
    - dependencies: Find dependencies for a file
    - search: Search nodes by pattern
    - stats: Show graph statistics

    Examples:
        python -m pyragify.cli query-graph --graph-path output/graphs/repository_graph.json --command related --entity "src/pyragify/graph.py::GraphBuilder"
        python -m pyragify.cli query-graph --graph-path output/graphs/repository_graph.json --command hierarchy --entity "add_node"
        python -m pyragify.cli query-graph --graph-path output/graphs/repository_graph.json --command dependencies --entity "src/pyragify/graph.py"
        python -m pyragify.cli query-graph --graph-path output/graphs/repository_graph.json --command search --pattern "function"
    """

    # Load the knowledge graph
    if not graph_path:
        # Try to find the default graph
        default_graph = Path("output/graphs/repository_graph.json")
        if default_graph.exists():
            graph_path = default_graph
        else:
            typer.echo("Error: No graph path provided and default graph not found.", err=True)
            raise typer.Exit(1)

    if not graph_path.exists():
        typer.echo(f"Error: Graph file '{graph_path}' not found.", err=True)
        raise typer.Exit(1)

    try:
        from pyragify.graph import KnowledgeGraph, GraphQuery

        # Load graph
        graph = KnowledgeGraph.from_dict(load_json(graph_path, "graph"))
        query = GraphQuery(graph)

        # Execute command
        if command == "related":
            if not entity:
                typer.echo("Error: --entity required for 'related' command", err=True)
                raise typer.Exit(1)

            results = query.find_related_context(entity, depth)
            if output_format == "json":
                import json
                output = {
                    "entity": entity,
                    "results": [
                        {
                            "node": {
                                "id": chunk.node.id,
                                "type": chunk.node.type,
                                "name": chunk.node.name,
                                "file": chunk.node.file
                            },
                            "relevance_score": chunk.relevance_score,
                            "relationship_path": chunk.relationship_path
                        } for chunk in results
                    ]
                }
                typer.echo(json.dumps(output, indent=2))
            else:
                typer.echo(f"Related context for {entity}:")
                for chunk in results:
                    relationships = " -> ".join(chunk.relationship_path)
                    typer.echo(f"  {chunk.node.name} ({chunk.node.type}) - Score: {chunk.relevance_score:.2f} - Relationships: {relationships}")

        elif command == "hierarchy":
            if not entity:
                typer.echo("Error: --entity required for 'hierarchy' command", err=True)
                raise typer.Exit(1)

            results = query.get_call_hierarchy(entity)
            if output_format == "json":
                import json
                typer.echo(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
            else:
                typer.echo(f"Call hierarchy for {entity}:")
                typer.echo(f"  Locations: {results['locations']}")
                typer.echo(f"  Callers: {[c['name'] for c in results['callers']]}")
                typer.echo(f"  Callees: {[c['name'] for c in results['callees']]}")

        elif command == "dependencies":
            if not entity:
                typer.echo("Error: --entity required for 'dependencies' command", err=True)
                raise typer.Exit(1)

            results = query.find_dependencies(entity)
            if output_format == "json":
                import json
                typer.echo(json.dumps({"file": entity, "dependencies": results}, indent=2))
            else:
                typer.echo(f"Dependencies for {entity}:")
                for dep in results:
                    typer.echo(f"  {dep}")

        elif command == "search":
            if not pattern:
                typer.echo("Error: --pattern required for 'search' command", err=True)
                raise typer.Exit(1)

            results = query.search_by_pattern(pattern)
            if output_format == "json":
                import json
                output = {
                    "pattern": pattern,
                    "results": [
                        {
                            "id": node.id,
                            "type": node.type,
                            "name": node.name,
                            "file": node.file
                        } for node in results
                    ]
                }
                typer.echo(json.dumps(output, indent=2))
            else:
                typer.echo(f"Search results for pattern '{pattern}':")
                for node in results:
                    typer.echo(f"  {node.name} ({node.type}) in {node.file}")

        elif command == "stats":
            # Use GraphBuilder to get statistics
            from pyragify.graph import GraphBuilder
            builder = GraphBuilder(Path("."))  # Dummy path, won't be used for stats
            builder.graph = graph
            stats = builder.get_statistics()

            if output_format == "json":
                import json
                typer.echo(json.dumps(stats, indent=2))
            else:
                typer.echo("Graph Statistics:")
                typer.echo(f"  Total nodes: {stats['total_nodes']}")
                typer.echo(f"  Total edges: {stats['total_edges']}")
                typer.echo(f"  Languages: {', '.join(stats['languages'])}")
                typer.echo("  Node types:")
                for node_type, count in stats['node_types'].items():
                    typer.echo(f"    {node_type}: {count}")
                typer.echo("  Edge types:")
                for edge_type, count in stats['edge_types'].items():
                    typer.echo(f"    {edge_type}: {count}")

        else:
            typer.echo(f"Error: Unknown command '{command}'", err=True)
            typer.echo("Available commands: related, hierarchy, dependencies, search, stats", err=True)
            raise typer.Exit(1)

    except typer.Exit:
        raise
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Error executing query: {e}")
        typer.echo(f"Error: {e}", err=True)
        raise typer.Exit(1)

def add_dependency_edges(
    self,
    graph: KnowledgeGraph,
    file_path: Path,
    language: str,
    dependencies: List[GraphEdge],
) -> None:
    """Normalize dependency endpoints, materialize missing nodes, and add edges."""
    file_node_id = self._file_node_id(file_path)
    python_definitions = {
        (node.line_start, node.metadata.get("column")): node.id
        for node in graph.nodes.values()
        if node.language == "python" and node.type in {"function", "class"}
    }
    javascript_definitions = {
        node.metadata["start_byte"]: node.id for node in graph.nodes.values()
        if node.language in {"javascript", "typescript"} and "start_byte" in node.metadata
    }
    for edge in dependencies:
        line = edge.metadata.get("line")
        if language == "python" and edge.type == "calls":
            owner = edge.metadata["owner"]
            definition = edge.metadata["definition"]
            source = python_definitions.get(tuple(owner), file_node_id) if owner else file_node_id
            target = python_definitions.get(tuple(definition), edge.target) if definition else edge.target
        elif language in {"javascript", "typescript"} and edge.type in {"calls", "inherits"}:
            source = javascript_definitions.get(edge.metadata.get("owner"), file_node_id)
            target = javascript_definitions.get(edge.metadata.get("definition"), edge.target)
        else:
            source = self._normalize_reference_id(graph, file_path, edge.source, line)
            target = self._normalize_reference_id(graph, file_path, edge.target, line)
            if edge.type == "calls":
                source = self._find_enclosing_node_id(graph, file_path, line) or file_node_id
        if edge.type == "inherits" and language not in {"javascript", "typescript"}:
            subclass = self._find_enclosing_node_id(
                graph, file_path, line, {"class", "java_class", "javascript_class", "cpp_class"})
            if subclass:
                source = subclass
                scope = graph.nodes[subclass].metadata["qualified_name"].rpartition(".")[0]
                symbol = edge.target.split("::", 1)[-1]
                target = self._lookup_local_node_id(graph, symbol, scope) or target

        edge.source = source
        edge.target = target
        self._ensure_reference_node(graph, edge.source, language)
        self._ensure_reference_node(graph, edge.target, language)
        graph.add_edge(edge)

def build_from_chunks(self, file_path: Path, chunks: List[Dict[str, Any]],
                     language: str) -> KnowledgeGraph:
    """
    Build graph from file chunks and their dependencies.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_path : Path
        Path to the file being processed
    chunks : List[Dict[str, Any]]
        List of code chunks from the file
    language : str
        Programming language of the file

    Returns
    -------
    KnowledgeGraph
        The constructed knowledge graph for this file
    """
    file_graph = KnowledgeGraph()
    relative_path = self._relative_path(file_path)

    # Create file node
    file_node = GraphNode(
        id=self._file_node_id(relative_path),
        type="file",
        file=relative_path,
        name=file_path.name,
        language=language,
        metadata={"size": file_path.stat().st_size}
    )
    file_graph.add_node(file_node)
    self.file_nodes[relative_path] = file_node

    # Process chunks and extract entities
    for chunk in sorted(chunks, key=lambda item: (item.get("start_line") or 0,
                                                item.get("metadata", {}).get("start_byte", 0))):
        self._process_chunk(chunk, relative_path, language, file_graph)

    return file_graph

def repair_graph(self, validation_results: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """
    Attempt to repair common graph issues found during validation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    validation_results : Dict[str, Any]
        Results from validate_graph() method
    """
    repairs_made = 0

    # Remove edges with non-existent nodes
    valid_edges = []
    node_ids = set(self.graph.nodes.keys())

    for edge in self.graph.edges:
        if edge.source in node_ids and edge.target in node_ids:
            valid_edges.append(edge)
        else:
            repairs_made += 1
            logger.debug(f"Removed invalid edge: {edge.source} -> {edge.target}")

    self.graph.edges = valid_edges

    # Remove duplicate edges (keep first occurrence)
    seen_signatures = set()
    deduplicated_edges = []

    for edge in self.graph.edges:
        signature = self.graph._edge_signature(edge)
        if signature not in seen_signatures:
            seen_signatures.add(signature)
            deduplicated_edges.append(edge)
        else:
            repairs_made += 1

    self.graph.edges = deduplicated_edges
    self.graph.sync_metadata()

    if repairs_made > 0:
        logger.info(f"Graph repair completed: {repairs_made} issues fixed")
    else:
        logger.info("Graph repair completed: no issues found")

def validate_graph(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Validate the knowledge graph for consistency and integrity.

    Returns
    -------
    Dict[str, Any]
        Validation results with errors, warnings, and statistics
    """
    validation_results = {
        "errors": [],
        "warnings": [],
        "statistics": self.get_statistics(),
        "is_valid": True
    }

    # Check for orphaned edges (edges referencing non-existent nodes)
    node_ids = set(self.graph.nodes.keys())
    for edge in self.graph.edges:
        if edge.source not in node_ids:
            validation_results["errors"].append(f"Edge source '{edge.source}' does not exist in nodes")
            validation_results["is_valid"] = False
        if edge.target not in node_ids:
            validation_results["errors"].append(f"Edge target '{edge.target}' does not exist in nodes")
            validation_results["is_valid"] = False

    # Check for duplicate edges
    edge_signatures = set()
    for edge in self.graph.edges:
        signature = self.graph._edge_signature(edge)
        if signature in edge_signatures:
            validation_results["warnings"].append(f"Duplicate edge: {signature}")
        else:
            edge_signatures.add(signature)

    # Check for nodes without required fields
    for node_id, node in self.graph.nodes.items():
        if not node.name:
            validation_results["warnings"].append(f"Node '{node_id}' has empty name")
        if not node.type:
            validation_results["errors"].append(f"Node '{node_id}' has empty type")
            validation_results["is_valid"] = False

    # Check for isolated nodes (nodes with no edges)
    connected_nodes = set()
    for edge in self.graph.edges:
        connected_nodes.add(edge.source)
        connected_nodes.add(edge.target)

    isolated_nodes = set(self.graph.nodes.keys()) - connected_nodes
    if isolated_nodes:
        validation_results["warnings"].append(f"Found {len(isolated_nodes)} isolated nodes")

    # Validate edge types
    valid_edge_types = {"imports", "calls", "inherits", "references", "contains",
                      "includes", "defines", "cross_file_reference"}
    for edge in self.graph.edges:
        if edge.type not in valid_edge_types:
            validation_results["warnings"].append(f"Unknown edge type: '{edge.type}'")

    logger.info(f"Graph validation completed: {len(validation_results['errors'])} errors, "
               f"{len(validation_results['warnings'])} warnings")

    return validation_results

def find_related_context(self, entity_id: str, depth: int = 2,
                       relationship_types: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> List[ContextChunk]:
    """
    Find related context for a given entity using breadth-first search.

    Parameters
    ----------
    entity_id : str
        The ID of the entity to find related context for
    depth : int, optional
        Maximum depth to traverse (default: 2)
    relationship_types : List[str], optional
        Types of relationships to follow (default: all)

    Returns
    -------
    List[ContextChunk]
        List of related context chunks with relevance scores
    """
    if entity_id not in self.graph.nodes:
        self.logger.warning(f"Entity {entity_id} not found in graph")
        return []

    if depth <= 0:
        return []

    adjacency = defaultdict(list)
    for edge in self.graph.edges:
        if relationship_types is not None and edge.type not in relationship_types:
            continue
        adjacency[edge.source].append(edge)
        if edge.target != edge.source:
            adjacency[edge.target].append(edge)

    visited = set()
    context_chunks = []

    # BFS traversal
    queue = deque([(entity_id, 0, [])])  # (node_id, current_depth, path)

    while queue:
        current_id, current_depth, path = queue.popleft()

        if current_id in visited or current_depth > depth:
            continue

        visited.add(current_id)
        current_node = self.graph.nodes[current_id]

        # Skip the original entity
        if current_id != entity_id:
            # Calculate relevance score based on depth and relationship type
            relevance_score = 1.0 / (current_depth + 1)
            if relationship_types and path and path[-1] not in relationship_types:
                relevance_score *= 0.5  # Reduce score for filtered relationships

            context_chunks.append(ContextChunk(
                node=current_node,
                relevance_score=relevance_score,
                relationship_path=path.copy(),
                metadata={"depth": current_depth}
            ))

        # Add neighbors to queue
        if current_depth < depth:
            for edge in adjacency.get(current_id, ()):
                neighbor_id = edge.target if edge.source == current_id else edge.source
                if neighbor_id not in visited:
                    queue.append((neighbor_id, current_depth + 1, path + [edge.type]))

    # Sort by relevance score
    context_chunks.sort(key=lambda x: x.relevance_score, reverse=True)
    return context_chunks

def get_call_hierarchy(self, function_name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Get the call hierarchy for a given function.

    Parameters
    ----------
    function_name : str
        Name of the function to analyze

    Returns
    -------
    Dict[str, Any]
        Call hierarchy with callers and callees
    """
    hierarchy = {
        "function": function_name,
        "callers": [],
        "callees": [],
        "locations": []
    }

    # Find all function nodes with this name
    function_nodes = []
    for node in self.graph.nodes.values():
        if is_function_like_node(node) and function_name in (
                node.name, node.metadata.get("qualified_name"), node.id):
            function_nodes.append(node)
            hierarchy["locations"].append({
                "file": node.file,
                "line": node.line_start
            })

    # Find callers and callees
    for node in function_nodes:
        # Find callers (functions that call this function)
        for edge in self.graph.edges:
            if edge.target == node.id and edge.type == "calls":
                caller_node = self.graph.nodes.get(edge.source)
                if caller_node and is_function_like_node(caller_node):
                    hierarchy["callers"].append({
                        "name": caller_node.name,
                        "file": caller_node.file,
                        "line": edge.metadata.get("line")
                    })

        # Find callees (functions called by this function)
        for edge in self.graph.edges:
            if edge.source == node.id and edge.type == "calls":
                callee_id = edge.target
                # Extract function name from target
                if "::" in callee_id:
                    callee_node = self.graph.nodes.get(callee_id)
                    callee_name = callee_node.name if callee_node else callee_id.split("::")[-1]
                    hierarchy["callees"].append({
                        "name": callee_name,
                        "line": edge.metadata.get("line")
                    })

    return hierarchy

    Search for nodes matching a pattern in their name or content.

        Types of nodes to search (default: all)

    -------
    List[GraphNode]
        List of matching nodes

    matching_nodes = []
    regex = re.compile(pattern, re.IGNORECASE)

    for node in self.graph.nodes.values():
        if node_types and node.type not in node_types:
            continue

        # Search in node name
        if regex.search(node.name):

        # Search in metadata
        for key, value in node.metadata.items():
            if isinstance(value, str) and regex.search(value):
                matching_nodes.append(node)
                break

    return matching_nodes

def from_dict(cls, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> 'KnowledgeGraph':
    """Create graph from dictionary (deserialization)."""
    if (not isinstance(data, dict)
            or not isinstance(data.get("nodes"), dict)
            or not isinstance(data.get("edges"), list)):
        raise ValueError("Graph must contain a nodes object and an edges list")
    graph = cls()
    graph.metadata = data.get("metadata", {}).copy()
    languages = graph.metadata.get("languages", set())
    if not isinstance(languages, set):
        graph.metadata["languages"] = set(languages or [])

    # Reconstruct nodes
    for node_id, node_data in data.get("nodes", {}).items():
        node = GraphNode(**node_data)
        graph.nodes[node_id] = node

    # Reconstruct edges
    for edge_data in data.get("edges", []):
        edge = GraphEdge(**edge_data)
        graph.edges.append(edge)

    graph.sync_metadata()
    return graph

def chunk_file(
    self,
    file_path: Path,
    include_graph: bool = False,
) -> Union[Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], int], Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], int, Optional[KnowledgeGraph]]]:
    """
    Retain one complete UTF-8 source block and optionally build a graph.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_path : pathlib.Path
        The path to the file to be chunked.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], int, Optional[KnowledgeGraph]]
        A tuple containing:
        - List of chunks (dict)
        - Total number of lines in the file (int)
        - Knowledge graph for the file (optional, only if graph building is enabled)

    Notes
    -----
    Source retention does not use parsers. Type-specific extractors are used
    only for the separate experimental graph; their failures do not remove source.
    """
    suffix = file_path.suffix
    language = FILE_TYPE_MAP.get(suffix, "unknown")

    try:
        content = file_path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
    except (OSError, UnicodeError) as e:
        logger.warning(f"Error reading file {file_path}: {e}")
        return ([], 0, None) if include_graph else ([], 0)
    line_count = sum(1 for _ in StringIO(content, newline=None))
    chunks = [{"type": "file", "name": file_path.name, "content": content,
               "start_line": 1 if content else 0, "end_line": line_count}]

    # Build graph if enabled
    graph = None
    if self.enable_graph and self.graph_builder:
        self.parser_limitations = chunks[0]["parser_limitations"] = [
            "Graph extraction is experimental and may omit symbols or relationships; source is retained verbatim."
        ]
        try:
            if suffix == ".py":
                graph_chunks, _ = self.chunk_python_file(file_path)
            elif suffix in {".md", ".markdown"}:
                graph_chunks, _ = self.chunk_markdown_file(file_path)
            elif suffix in FILE_TYPE_MAP:
                graph_chunks, _ = self.chunk_tree_sitter_file(file_path, suffix)
            else:
                graph_chunks = chunks
            graph = self.graph_builder.build_from_chunks(file_path, graph_chunks, language)

            # Extract additional dependencies from file content
            try:
                dependencies = self.graph_builder.extract_dependencies(file_path, content, language)
                self.graph_builder.add_dependency_edges(graph, file_path, language, dependencies)
            except Exception as e:
                self.parser_limitations.append(f"Graph dependencies failed: {e}")
                logger.warning(f"Error extracting dependencies from {file_path}: {e}")

            logger.debug(f"Built knowledge graph for {file_path} with {len(graph.nodes)} nodes and {len(graph.edges)} edges")
        except Exception as e:
            chunks[0]["parser_limitations"].append(str(e))
            logger.warning(f"Error building graph for {file_path}: {e}")

    if include_graph:
        return chunks, line_count, graph
    return chunks, line_count

def chunk_markdown_file(self, file_path: Path) -> tuple[list, int]:
    """
    Chunk a Markdown file into sections based on headers.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_path : pathlib.Path
        The path to the Markdown file to be chunked.

    Returns
    -------
    list of dict
        A list of dictionaries where each dictionary represents a chunk with a header and its associated content.

    Notes
    -----
    Each chunk contains the following keys:
    - 'header': The header text (e.g., '# Title').
    - 'content': The content under the header.
    """

    chunks = []
    try:
        with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
        line_count = len(lines)

        current_chunk = {"type": "markdown", "header": None, "name": file_path.stem, "content": ""}
        heading_stack: List[str] = []
        in_code_block = False

        for line_number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
            if MARKDOWN_FENCE_RE.match(line):
                in_code_block = not in_code_block
                current_chunk["content"] += line
                continue

            header_match = MARKDOWN_HEADER_RE.match(line) if not in_code_block else None
            if header_match:
                if current_chunk["header"] or current_chunk["content"].strip():
                    chunks.append(current_chunk)

                level = len(header_match.group(1))
                title = header_match.group(2).strip()
                heading_stack = heading_stack[:level - 1]
                heading_stack.append(title)

                current_chunk = {
                    "type": "markdown",
                    "header": line.strip(),
                    "name": " > ".join(heading_stack),
                    "content": "",
                    "start_line": line_number,
                }
            else:
                current_chunk["content"] += line
        if current_chunk["header"] or current_chunk["content"].strip():
            chunks.append(current_chunk)
    except Exception as e:
        self.parser_limitations.append(f"Markdown graph extraction failed: {e}")
        logger.warning(f"Error chunking Markdown file {file_path}: {e}")
    return chunks, line_count if 'line_count' in locals() else 0

def chunk_python_file(self, file_path: Path) -> tuple[list, int]:
    """
    Chunk a Python file into semantic sections, including code, functions, and comments.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_path : pathlib.Path
        The path to the Python file to be chunked.

    Returns
    -------
    list of dict
        A list of dictionaries where each dictionary represents a chunk with metadata and content.

    Notes
    -----
    The chunks include functions, classes, and inline comments. Each chunk contains the following keys:
    - 'type': The type of the chunk (e.g., 'function', 'class', 'comments').
    - 'name': The name of the function or class (if applicable).
    - 'docstring': The docstring associated with the function or class.
    - 'code': The actual code of the function or class.
    - 'line_count': The number of lines in the file.
    """

    chunks = []
    try:
        with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            file_content = f.read()

        lines = file_content.splitlines()
        line_count = len(lines)

        # Extract functions and classes using AST
        tree = ast.parse(file_content, filename=file_path)
        for node in ast.walk(tree):
            if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
                func_name = node.name
                code_snippet = ast.get_source_segment(file_content, node)
                chunks.append({
                    "type": "function",
                    "name": func_name,
                    "docstring": ast.get_docstring(node),
                    "code": code_snippet,
                    "start_line": node.lineno,
                    "end_line": node.end_lineno,
                    "metadata": {"column": node.col_offset, "end_column": node.end_col_offset},
                })
            elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
                if not hasattr(node, 'end_lineno'): continue # Skip nodes without end line info
                class_name = node.name
                code_snippet = ast.get_source_segment(file_content, node)
                methods = []
                for class_node in node.body:
                    if isinstance(class_node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
                        method_name = class_node.name
                        methods.append({
                            "name": method_name,
                        })
                chunks.append({
                    "type": "class",
                    "name": class_name,
                    "methods": methods,
                    "docstring": ast.get_docstring(node),
                    "code": code_snippet,
                    "start_line": node.lineno,
                    "end_line": node.end_lineno,
                    "metadata": {"column": node.col_offset, "end_column": node.end_col_offset},
                })

        # Extract inline comments using tokenize
        tokens = tokenize.generate_tokens(StringIO(file_content).readline)
        comments = []
        for token in tokens:
            if token.type == tokenize.COMMENT:
                line_number = token.start[0]
                comment_text = token.string.lstrip("#").strip()
                comments.append({
                    "type": "comment",
                    "line": line_number,
                    "text": comment_text
                })
        if comments:
            chunks.append({"type": "comments", "name": "Comments", "content": comments})

    except Exception as e:
        self.parser_limitations.append(f"Python graph extraction failed: {e}")
        logger.warning(f"Error chunking Python file {file_path}: {e}")
    return chunks, line_count if 'line_count' in locals() else 0

def chunk_tree_sitter_file(self, file_path: Path, suffix: str) -> tuple[list, int]:
    """
    Chunk a file using tree-sitter for supported languages.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_path : pathlib.Path
        The path to the file to be chunked.
    suffix : str
        The file suffix (extension) to determine the language.

    Returns
    -------
    list of dict
        A list of dictionaries, each representing a semantic chunk with keys like 'type', 'name', and 'code' or 'content'.

    Notes
    -----
    Supports semantic extraction for JavaScript/TypeScript (functions, classes, arrow functions), Java (methods, classes), C/C++ (functions, structs), HTML (scripts, styles), and CSS (rules). Falls back to full content if parsing fails.
    """
    try:
        source = file_path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
        line_count = source.count('\n') + 1
        lang_name = FILE_TYPE_MAP[suffix]

        chunks = []

        # Try tree-sitter parsing first
        try:
            language, parser = get_tree_sitter_language_and_parser(lang_name)
            tree = parser.parse(bytes(source, "utf8"))
            root_node = tree.root_node
            if root_node.has_error:
                self.parser_limitations.append(f"Tree-sitter {lang_name} syntax errors; graph extraction may be incomplete.")

            if lang_name in ["javascript", "typescript"]:
                chunks.extend(_JavaScriptAnalysis(root_node).chunks)

            elif lang_name == "java":
                chunks.extend(self._query_tree_sitter(language, root_node, source,
                    "(method_declaration name: (identifier) @name) @method_declaration", "java_method"))
                chunks.extend(self._query_tree_sitter(language, root_node, source,
                    "(class_declaration name: (identifier) @name) @class_declaration", "java_class"))

            elif lang_name in ["cpp", "c"]:
                chunks.extend(self._query_tree_sitter(language, root_node, source, '''
                (function_definition
                  declarator: (function_declarator
                    declarator: (identifier) @name
                  )
                ) @function_definition
                ''', "cpp_function"))

                # Struct/Class for C++
                if lang_name == "cpp":
                    chunks.extend(self._query_tree_sitter(language, root_node, source, '''
                        (struct_specifier name: (type_identifier) @name) @struct_specifier
                    ''', "cpp_struct"))
                    chunks.extend(self._query_tree_sitter(language, root_node, source, '''
                        (class_specifier name: (type_identifier) @name) @class_specifier
                    ''', "cpp_class"))

            elif lang_name == "go":
                chunks.extend(self._query_tree_sitter(language, root_node, source, '''
                    (function_declaration
                      name: (identifier) @name
                    ) @function_declaration
                ''', "go_function"))
                chunks.extend(self._query_tree_sitter(language, root_node, source, '''
                    (type_declaration
                      (type_spec name: (type_identifier) @name)
                    ) @type
                ''', "go_type"))

        except Exception as e:
            self.parser_limitations.append(f"Tree-sitter {lang_name} graph extraction failed: {e}")
            logger.warning(f"Tree-sitter parsing failed for {lang_name}: {e}")

        # Fallback to regex for HTML/CSS or if tree-sitter failed
        if not chunks:
            if lang_name == "html":
                # Simple regex fallback for tags
                import re
                scripts = re.findall(r'<script[^>]*>(.*?)</script>', source, re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
                for script in scripts:
                    chunks.append({"type": "html_script", "content": script.strip()})
                styles = re.findall(r'<style[^>]*>(.*?)</style>', source, re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
                for style in styles:
                    chunks.append({"type": "html_style", "content": style.strip()})
                if not chunks:
                    chunks = [{"type": "html", "content": source}]

            # CSS: Chunk by rules
            elif lang_name == "css":
                import re
                rules = re.split(r'([@][^{]+{[^}]*}|{[^{}]*})', source)
                for rule in rules:
                    if rule.strip() and '{' in rule:
                        chunks.append({"type": "css_rule", "content": rule.strip()})
                if not chunks:
                    chunks = [{"type": "css", "content": source}]

            else:
                # For other languages, fall back to full file content
                chunks = [{"type": "file", "name": file_path.name, "content": source}]

        return chunks, line_count
    except Exception as e:
        self.parser_limitations.append(f"{suffix} graph extraction failed: {e}")
        logger.warning(f"Error chunking {suffix} file {file_path}: {e}")
        content = file_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        return [{"type": "file", "name": file_path.name, "content": content}], content.count('\n') + 1

def format_chunk(self, chunk: dict, file_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Format a chunk into plain text for saving.

    Parameters
    ----------
    chunk : dict
        The chunk of content to format.
    file_path : str
        The relative path of the file the chunk belongs to.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        A formatted plain-text representation of the chunk.
    """
    chunk_type = chunk.get("type", "unknown")
    if chunk_type == "file":
        content = chunk["content"]
        fence = "`" * max(3, max((len(run) + 1 for run in re.findall(r"`+", content)), default=3))
        anchor = "source-" + file_path.encode("utf-8").hex()
        # Keep the source intact, including its final newline (or lack of one).
        display_path = html.escape(json.dumps(file_path, ensure_ascii=False)[1:-1])
        return (f'<a id="{anchor}"></a>\n\n### File: {display_path}\n\n'
                f'Lines: {chunk["start_line"]}-{chunk["end_line"]}\n\n'
                f'{fence}{FILE_TYPE_MAP.get(Path(file_path).suffix, "text")}\n'
                f'{content}\n{fence}')
    name = chunk.get("name")
    start_line = chunk.get("start_line")
    end_line = chunk.get("end_line")
    lines_str = f"{start_line}-{end_line}" if start_line and end_line else None

    # Helper to create a metadata header
    def create_header(display_type: str):
        parts = ["---", f"File: {file_path}", f"Type: {display_type}"]
        if name:
            parts.append(f"Name: {name}")
        if chunk_type == "markdown" and chunk.get("header"):
            parts.append(f"Header: {chunk['header']}")
        if lines_str:
            parts.append(f"Lines: {lines_str}")
        return "\n".join(parts) + "\n---\n\n"

    # Generic code chunk formatting
    if "code" in chunk:
        docstring = chunk.get("docstring")
        code = chunk.get("code", "")
        lang = FILE_TYPE_MAP.get(Path(file_path).suffix, chunk_type.split('_')[0])
        display_type = chunk_type.replace('_', ' ').title()

        header = create_header(display_type)
        title = f"### {display_type}: `{name}`\n\n"
        docstring_md = f"**Docstring:**\n> {docstring}\n\n" if docstring else ""
        code_md = f"**Code:**\n```{lang}\n{code.strip()}\n```"
        return f"{header}{title}{docstring_md}{code_md}"

    # Fallback for content-based chunks (like full files or markdown sections)
    elif "content" in chunk:
        content = chunk.get("content", "")
        suffix = Path(file_path).suffix
        lang = FILE_TYPE_MAP.get(suffix, "text")
        if chunk_type == "file":
            display_type = "File Content"
        elif chunk_type == "markdown":
            display_type = "Markdown Section"
        else:
            display_type = chunk_type.replace('_', ' ').title()
        header = create_header(display_type)
        title = f"### {chunk.get('name') or chunk.get('header') or display_type}\n\n"

        # Handle different content types
        if isinstance(content, list):
            # For comments or other list-based content
            if chunk_type == "comments":
                content_md = "\n".join(f"- Line {c['line']}: {c['text']}" for c in content)
            else:
                content_md = "\n".join(str(item) for item in content)
        else:
            # For string content
            content_md = f"```{lang}\n{content.strip()}\n```" if chunk_type == "file" else content.strip()

        return f"{header}{title}{content_md}"

    else:
        return f"---\nFile: {file_path}\nType: {chunk_type.title()}\n---\n\n{chunk}"

def __init__(self, repo_path: Path, output_dir: Path, max_words: int = 200000, max_file_size: int = 10 * 1024 * 1024, skip_patterns: list = None, skip_dirs: list = None, enable_graph: bool = False, graph_config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None):
    if max_words <= 0:
        raise ValueError("max_words must be positive")
    self.repo_path = repo_path.resolve()
    self.output_dir = self._validate_output_path(output_dir)
    self.graph_config = graph_config or {}
    unsupported = set(self.graph_config) - {"enabled", "output_dir", "format"}
    if enable_graph and (unsupported or self.graph_config.get("format", "json") != "json"):
        raise ValueError("Only JSON graph output is supported; unsupported settings: "
                         f"{sorted(unsupported) or ['format']}")
    self.graph_output_dir = self._validate_output_path(
        self.output_dir / self.graph_config.get("output_dir", "graphs")
    ) if enable_graph else None
    self._gitignore_specs = {}
    self.max_words = max_words
    self.max_file_size = max_file_size
    self.skip_patterns = list(dict.fromkeys(DEFAULT_SKIP_PATTERNS + (skip_patterns or [])))
    self.skip_dirs = skip_dirs or ["node_modules", "__pycache__"]
    self.ignore_patterns = self.load_ignore_patterns()
    self.current_word_counts = defaultdict(int)
    self.content_buffers = defaultdict(str)
    self.hashes = {}
    self.cache_path = self.output_dir / CACHE_FILENAME
    self._reject_symlinks(self.cache_path)
    try:
        self.file_cache = load_json(self.cache_path, "File cache")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        self.file_cache = {}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        logger.warning("Invalid optional cache; processing source again")
        self.file_cache = {}
    self.file_counter = defaultdict(int)
    self.metadata = self._empty_metadata()

    # Graph-related attributes
    self.enable_graph = enable_graph
    self.graph_config = graph_config or {}
    self.repo_graph = None
    self.all_file_graphs = []  # Store all individual file graphs

    if self.enable_graph:
        from pyragify.graph import KnowledgeGraph
        self.repo_graph = KnowledgeGraph()
        logger.info("Repository graph building enabled")

    self.file_processor = FileProcessor(self.repo_path, self.output_dir, enable_graph=enable_graph, graph_config=graph_config)

    validate_directory(self.output_dir)

def load_ignore_patterns(self) -> pathspec.PathSpec:
    """
    Load root .dockerignore and configured skip patterns.

    Returns
    -------
    pathspec.PathSpec
        A compiled PathSpec object containing all ignore patterns.

    Notes
    -----
    Additional patterns provided via `skip_patterns` are also included. 
    If the ignore files are missing, only the additional patterns are used.
    """

    ignore_patterns = []

    for ignore_file in [".dockerignore"]:
        file_path = self.repo_path / ignore_file
        if file_path.exists() and not file_path.is_symlink():
            logger.info(f"Loading ignore patterns from {ignore_file}")
            with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                ignore_patterns.extend(f.readlines())

    # Add additional skip_patterns
    ignore_patterns.extend(self.skip_patterns)

    # Compile patterns using pathspec
    return pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", ignore_patterns)

def process_repo(self):
    """
    Process all files in the repository in parallel.

    The per-file cache avoids re-chunking unchanged files, but output is
    always rebuilt from the complete cached model so incremental runs do
    not drop unchanged files from the generated model.
    """
    logger.info(f"Processing repository: {self.repo_path}")
    self._reset_run_state()
    self._gitignore_specs.clear()

    # 1. Discover files and decide which ones need fresh processing.
    logger.info("Discovering and filtering files...")
    active_records = {}
    cache_files = self._cache_files()
    files_to_process = []

    for file_path in self._discover_files():
        if not file_path.is_symlink() and not file_path.is_file():
            if file_path.is_dir():
                self.metadata["skipped_files"].append({
                    "path": file_path.relative_to(self.repo_path).as_posix() + "/",
                    "reason": "Nested repository or submodule boundary"})
            continue
        if self._is_inside_output_dir(file_path):
            logger.debug(f"Skipped generated output artifact: {file_path}")
            continue
        if self.should_skip(file_path):
            relative_path = str(file_path.relative_to(self.repo_path))
            if not any(entry["path"] == relative_path for entry in self.metadata["skipped_files"]):
                self.metadata["skipped_files"].append({"path": relative_path, "reason": "Skipped by pattern or size"})
            continue

        current_hash = compute_file_hash(file_path)
        if not current_hash:
            self.metadata["failed_files"].append({"path": str(file_path.relative_to(self.repo_path)), "reason": "Error computing file hash"})
            logger.warning(f"Skipped file due to hash error: {file_path}")
            continue

        relative_path = str(file_path.relative_to(self.repo_path))
        cache_record = cache_files.get(relative_path)
        if self._is_cache_record_usable(cache_record, current_hash, relative_path):
            active_records[relative_path] = cache_record
            self.metadata["reused_files"].append(relative_path)
            logger.debug(f"Reused cached chunks for unchanged file: {file_path}")
            continue

        files_to_process.append(file_path)

    if not files_to_process:
        logger.info("No new or modified files to process.")
    else:
        logger.info(f"Found {len(files_to_process)} new or modified files to process.")
        # 2. Process new or modified files in parallel.
        tasks = [(str(fp), str(self.repo_path), str(self.output_dir), self.enable_graph, self.graph_config) for fp in files_to_process]
        with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=cpu_count()) as executor:
            results = executor.map(_process_file_worker, tasks)
            for i, result in enumerate(results):
                source_path = files_to_process[i]
                relative_source_path = str(source_path.relative_to(self.repo_path))
                if result is None:
                    logger.warning("A worker failed to process a file.")
                    self.metadata["failed_files"].append({"path": relative_source_path, "reason": "Error processing file"})
                    continue

                relative_path, new_hash, file_metadata, chunks, graph_dict = result
                logger.info(f"Aggregating results for {relative_path} ({i + 1}/{len(files_to_process)})")
                active_records[relative_path] = {
                    "hash": new_hash,
                    "metadata": file_metadata,
                    "chunks": chunks,
                    "graph": graph_dict,
                }

    if self.metadata["failed_files"]:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Source processing failed: {self.metadata['failed_files']}")

    # 3. Rebuild aggregate output from every active source record.
    self.hashes = {
        relative_path: record["hash"]
        for relative_path, record in sorted(active_records.items())
    }
    self._record_processed_metadata(active_records)
    self._rebuild_graph_from_records(active_records)

    # 4. Resolve cross-file references
    if self.enable_graph and self.repo_graph and self.all_file_graphs:
        try:
            from pyragify.graph import GraphBuilder
            graph_builder = GraphBuilder(self.repo_path)
            graph_builder.graph = self.repo_graph
            graph_builder.resolve_cross_file_references(self.all_file_graphs)
            logger.info("Cross-file reference resolution completed")

            # Validate and repair the graph
            validation_results = graph_builder.validate_graph()
            if not validation_results["is_valid"] or validation_results["warnings"]:
                logger.info("Graph validation found issues, attempting repair...")
                graph_builder.repair_graph(validation_results)

                # Re-validate after repair
                final_validation = graph_builder.validate_graph()
                if final_validation["is_valid"]:
                    logger.info("Graph repair successful")
                else:
                    logger.warning("Some graph issues could not be repaired")

        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Failed to resolve cross-file references: {e}")

    # 5. Save final state
    self.file_cache = {"version": CACHE_VERSION, "files": active_records}

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".pyragify-stage-", dir=self.output_dir) as directory:
        stage = Path(directory)
        output_dir = self.output_dir
        try:
            self.output_dir = stage
            self._write_text_output(active_records)
        finally:
            self.output_dir = output_dir
        if self.enable_graph and self.repo_graph:
            graph_dict = self.repo_graph.to_dict()
            save_json(graph_dict, stage / "repository_graph.json", "Repository graph")
            self.metadata["graph"] = graph_dict["metadata"].copy()
            self.metadata["graph"]["output_path"] = str(self.graph_output_dir / "repository_graph.json")
        save_json(self.metadata, stage / "metadata.json", "Metadata")
        save_json(self.hashes, stage / "hashes.json", "Hashes")
        save_json(self.file_cache, stage / CACHE_FILENAME, "File cache")
        self._publish_output(stage)

    logger.info("Repository processing complete.")

def save_chunk(self, chunk: dict, subdir: Path, file_path: str) -> dict:
    """
    Buffer a formatted chunk within the word limit and return its output mapping.

    Parameters
    ----------
    chunk : dict
        The chunk of content to save.
    subdir : pathlib.Path
        The subdirectory where the chunk should be saved.
    file_path : str
        The relative path of the file the chunk belongs to.
    """
    formatted = self.file_processor.format_chunk(chunk, file_path)
    chunk_word_count = len(formatted.split())
    if chunk_word_count > self.max_words:
        raise ValueError(f"{file_path} needs {chunk_word_count} words including headers; "
                         f"max_words={self.max_words}. Increase the limit or exclude this file.")
    if self.current_word_counts[subdir] + chunk_word_count > self.max_words:
        self.save_content(subdir)
    output = {"part": f"{subdir}/chunk_{self.file_counter[subdir]}.md"}
    if chunk.get("type") == "file":
        # The last line is the closing fence; offsets exclude its framing newline.
        end = len((self.content_buffers[subdir] + formatted.rsplit("\n", 1)[0]).encode("utf-8"))
        output.update({"anchor": "source-" + file_path.encode("utf-8").hex(),
                       "start_line": chunk["start_line"], "end_line": chunk["end_line"],
                       "start_byte": end - len(chunk["content"].encode("utf-8")), "end_byte": end})
    self.content_buffers[subdir] += formatted + "\n\n"
    self.current_word_counts[subdir] += chunk_word_count
    return output

def save_content(self, subdir: Path):
    """
    Save the accumulated content to a file.

    This method writes the currently accumulated content to a file in the specified subdirectory.
    After saving, the content and word count are reset for the next chunk.

    Parameters
    ----------
    subdir : pathlib.Path
        The subdirectory within the output directory where the chunk file should be saved.

    Notes
    -----
    - The file is named `chunk_<counter>.md`, where `<counter>` is an incrementing number for the subdirectory.
    - If the subdirectory does not exist, it is created automatically.
    - Once the content is saved, the internal buffer (`self.content`) and the current word count (`self.current_word_count`) are reset to prepare for the next chunk.

    --------

        >>> processor = RepoContentProcessor(repo_path=Path("repo"), output_dir=Path("output"))

        >>> processor.current_word_count = 5
        >>> processor.save_content(Path("python"))

    Raises
    ------
    OSError
        If the file cannot be created or written, an error is logged.

    if self.content_buffers[subdir]:

def should_skip(self, file_path: Path) -> bool:
    """
    Determine if a file or directory should be skipped based on patterns.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_path : pathlib.Path
        The path to the file or directory to check.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True if the file or directory should be skipped, otherwise False.

    Notes
    -----
    This method checks against ignore patterns and explicit directory or file size limits.
    """

    relative_path = file_path.relative_to(self.repo_path)
    if any(part.is_symlink() for part in (file_path, *file_path.parents)):
        return True
    if self._matches_gitignore(file_path):
        return True

    # Skip files contained in explicitly skipped directories.
    if any(part in self.skip_dirs for part in relative_path.parts[:-1]):
        logger.debug(f"Skipped path inside configured skip directory: {file_path}")
        return True

    # Check if the path matches .gitignore or .dockerignore patterns
    if self.ignore_patterns.match_file(relative_path.as_posix() + ("/" if file_path.is_dir() else "")):
        logger.debug(f"Skipping {relative_path} due to ignore pattern.")
        return True

    # Skip directories explicitly listed
    if file_path.is_dir() and file_path.name in self.skip_dirs:
        logger.debug(f"Skipped directory: {file_path}")
        return True

    # Skip large files
    if file_path.is_file() and file_path.stat().st_size > self.max_file_size:
        self.metadata["skipped_files"].append({
            "path": str(file_path.relative_to(self.repo_path)),
            "reason": "File exceeds size limit"
        })
        logger.debug(f"Skipped file due to size: {file_path}")
        return True

    if file_path.is_file() and is_probably_binary_file(file_path):
        self.metadata["skipped_files"].append({
            "path": str(file_path.relative_to(self.repo_path)),
            "reason": "Binary or image file"
        })
        logger.debug(f"Skipped binary/image file: {file_path}")
        return True

    return False

def compute_file_hash(file_path: Path) -> str:
    """
    Compute the MD5 hash of a file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_path : pathlib.Path
        The path to the file whose hash is to be computed.

    Returns
    -------
    str or None
        The MD5 hash of the file as a hexadecimal string, or None if an error occurs.

    Raises
    ------
    Exception
        If the file cannot be read, the error is logged and None is returned.

    Notes
    -----
    MD5 is not suitable for cryptographic purposes but is sufficient for file integrity checks.
    """

    hash_md5 = hashlib.md5()
    try:
        with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
            for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(4096), b""):
                hash_md5.update(chunk)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Error computing hash for {file_path}: {e}")
        return None
    return hash_md5.hexdigest()

def is_probably_binary_file(file_path: Path, sample_size: int = 2048) -> bool:
    """Heuristically detect binary files so they can be skipped before decoding."""
    try:
        with open(file_path, "rb") as file:
            sample = file.read(sample_size + 1)
            complete = len(sample) <= sample_size
            sample = sample[:sample_size]
    except OSError:
        return False

    if not sample:
        return False

    if b"\x00" in sample:
        return True

    try:
        codecs.getincrementaldecoder("utf-8")().decode(sample, final=complete)
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return True

    return False

def read_file_in_chunks(file_path: Path, chunk_size: int = 4096):
    """
    Read a file in chunks to handle large files efficiently.

    -----
    This function is useful for processing very large files without loading them entirely into memory.
    """

    with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        while chunk := file.read(chunk_size):
            yield chunk

def save_json(data: dict, file_path: Path, description: str):
    """Atomically save JSON; serialization and filesystem errors propagate."""
    temporary = None
